source.title: A Resizable Mini-batch Gradient Descent based on a Multi-Armed Bandit
source.authors: S. Cho; Sunghun Kang; C. Yoo

record.tranche_reason: Compares fixed batch sizes on natural image classification with test accuracy, bearing on whether larger batches worsen held-out performance. It does not measure the train–test error gap directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy for fixed batch sizes and an adaptive batch-size method. Rows cover fixed-size MGD results and RMGD results reported in the tables. Background claims about prior studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: Fixed-batch comparisons measure held-out image-classification accuracy under equal epoch budgets, directly testing V5. Training accuracy or a train–test gap is unnecessary for this version. The study is not an original source.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: RMGD selects useful batch sizes and achieves or exceeds the best fixed-grid mean on MNIST and CIFAR10 while taking less time than the full grid search. Evidence for improvement is significant for Adam MNIST and CIFAR10, but not Adagrad MNIST. The authors' interpretation of p=0.155 as an 84.5% success probability is not justified.
record.recipe_differences: Compares fixed MGD batch sizes under fixed epoch counts, but does not evaluate training–test error gaps; also tests an adaptive bandit batch-size method.
record.method_sensitivity: The better-performing batch-size range differs by dataset: smaller sizes perform better on MNIST, while larger sizes perform better on CIFAR10. The reported optimizer conditions also differ by dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: RMGD exceeds the best fixed-batch mean by 0.014 points on Adam MNIST, 0.009 on Adagrad MNIST, and 0.107 on CIFAR10; respective reported p-values are 0.019, 0.155 and 0.002.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Validation-guided batch selection can match or improve fixed-batch grid-search accuracy while taking less total time than the grid search.

record.problems: No train accuracy or train–test gap is reported, so the study cannot directly measure the generalization gap. Results concern MNIST and CIFAR10 models and training recipes only.
record.rows_left_out: No eligible test-accuracy table rows left out.

untested.parts: Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under comparable tuning; MNIST compares only two adaptive optimizers.

Language models; longer training; warmup; controlled normalization or regularization changes; batch sizes beyond 512 on MNIST or 256 on CIFAR10; whether learning-rate scaling removes a penalty relative to an unscaled control.
Dropout ablation; dropout is used without a comparison removing it.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relationship to generalization gaps.

record.verdict_notes: The CIFAR10 recipe scales learning rate as 0.05 × batch_size/256 and decays it at epochs 200, 250 and 300. Fixed-batch pairwise significance tests are not reported; Table 5 tests RMGD comparisons only. Similar performance at intermediate batch sizes does not challenge a claim whose threshold is workload dependent.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Train–test error gaps; language models; other large-batch recipes including longer training, normalization, and regularization changes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures of the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring resulting test accuracy.

relationships.condition: MNIST simple CNN, Adam or Adagrad, 100 epochs, fixed learning rate within optimizer, batches 256–512 versus 16–64
relationships.reason: R5–R6 and R12–R13 show lower accuracy at the largest batches; batch 512 loses 0.073 points with Adam and 0.070 with Adagrad relative to batch 16, across 100 runs.

tranche.reason: Fixed-batch comparisons use the method and measure named by V5: vary batch size, hold epochs fixed, and measure held-out classification accuracy. The adaptive-method experiments do not remove these direct tests.
